source_evidence_statements: research/feedback_control_20261028.md describes neural direct suppression as predicting a mask or enhanced speech from howling microphone audio, trained on closed-loop signals representative of inference, and warns that offline open-loop training can mismatch recursive streaming behaviour and suppress target speech.

the same note reports Hybrid AHS (Interspeech 2023) as a frequency-domain Kalman filter plus a self-attentive RNN whose streaming NN output becomes the Kalman reference, and the expanded AHS journal study (2024) compares cascaded and recursively trained variants including a complex-ratio-mask system.

the same note records that HybridAHS v2 complex-ratio-mask results are the strongest overall trade-off in parts of the study, and reports NeuralKalmanAHS mean SDR 2.65, 1.98 and 1.45 dB with PESQ 2.33, 2.17 and 2.04 for loop gains G=2, 2.5 and 3 over 200 utterances on the paper setup only.

the same note records that YIXUANZ/NeuralKalmanAHS and YIXUANZ/AHS_2023 expose README/demo HTML, CSS and audio files with no source implementation or model checkpoints in their visible file listings and no release assets for NeuralKalmanAHS, so they are research references rather than runnable candidates.

the same note records AFC-SPEX (ICASSP 2026) as a three-microphone neural AFC candidate whose checked-in inference configuration expects an author-local checkpoint and whose repository listing includes no checkpoint; our AMI source is mono and it was not run.
